quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign warn about?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Road curve ahead.
Right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when using roundabouts or traffic circles?

options.text: Slow down as you approach the circle.
Yield to traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists already in the circle.
Enter to the right and steer left to go around counterclockwise.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a roundabout. Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already in the circle. Enter to your right but steer left to move around the circle counterclockwise.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see ahead clearly, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What should you do to pass safely on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn while passing.
Flash your headlights while passing.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes and the road is clear before you pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking ahead.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a steep hill ahead.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: An adult can safely hold them.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not get hurt because they are small.
They must never stand in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must never stand in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are made for small children. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper child seat to keep children safe.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: Must a driver turning left at an intersection yield to an oncoming bicycle?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be prepared to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your headlights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one taillight.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Check your side mirror, rearview mirror, and blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross first if they are in a crosswalk or about to enter one. Watch for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers that:

options.text: The right lane is ending and you must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are intersections coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and you must merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that the number of lanes is decreasing and traffic must move left.

questions.question: A solid green light at an intersection means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic first.
May go through the intersection if it is clear.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A solid green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection when turning.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stay near the accident scene and move your vehicle to the side of the road if possible.
Report the accident to police within one week.
Find a phone and call for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay near the accident scene and move your vehicle to the side of the road if possible.
questions.explanation: In an accident, stop your vehicle and move it off the road if you can. Help anyone who is hurt. Call the police right away. Exchange information with other drivers. Report the accident to your insurance company and the DMV.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line in the center of the road means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no vehicles from either direction can cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to dangers.
Often causes risky driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes risky driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.question: When a bus signals to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus returning to the road after loading or unloading passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do at a broken traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
You don't need to stop if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat it as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or lights, you should:

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Lower your radio volume to listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger's signal if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when sure no train is coming. Lower your radio to listen. Follow any flagger's instructions.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: Long trucks need extra space to turn right because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than their front wheels. They often must swing wide.

questions.question: Who is subject to South Carolina's Point System?

options.text: Permit holders
All drivers
Intermediate drivers only
Drivers over 65 years old

questions.correctAnswerText: All drivers
questions.explanation: A driver's license is a privilege that must be earned and kept. Your license will be suspended if you get 12 points for violations in or out of state.

questions.question: The driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or less.
Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for all pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Never pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.
